eligibility.quote: I've found the issue. Actually the default ROS2 humble DDS is fine. I forgot that I had specific DDS setting in my `~/.bashrc` (`FASTRTPS_DEFAULT_PROFILES_FILE`), based on the accepted answer of https://answers.ros.org/question/370595/ros2-foxy-nodes-cant-communicate-through-docker-container-border/ for an issue I had a couple of months ago that nodes between host and docker containers couldn't talk to each other. By removing that specific config and by re-running the test above, I have now similar results than with ROS1 ... Closing this issue as solved.

notes: Independently verified: issue #727 body (tf2_buffer_lag reproducer: camera_node 1920x1080 @30 Hz, broadcaster_node odom->base_link @30 Hz, listener_node lookupTransform with 0.5 s timeout from image callback, `stress -c 16`; the two log lines quoted in the spec appear verbatim; E4 quote "In this example, for almost 3 seconds of TF waiting, the TF Buffer didn't get updated once." confirmed); reporter's resolution comment 2481510627 confirmed verbatim; the withdrawal of the per-RMW comparison ("I didn't re-rerun the test on all other DDS, maybe that config also affected their results") confirmed; rtabmap_ros PR #1225 body does reference this issue (grep hit) and its title "ROS2 various QOL updates (preparing new binary release)" matches the spec's claim that it is not a fix of this composition. My independent reading: the minimal resolving change removed a user-shell environment variable selecting a Fast DDS transport profile — purely deployment-environment configuration, no unit's code or declared/referenced interface changed, and the source never identifies a wrong element crossing the broadcaster/listener boundary. That is deployment wiring in substance, so I stop at step 3 as the spec does; the spec's own note that internal@2 (delay in the listener's own middleware receive path, any correct /tf publisher) is an equally defensible strict-text reading is fair, but either stop yields ineligible, so the recorded decision stands.
